extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents and other persons doing business before the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formatting requirements for written communications, electronic submissions, and related interactions with the Canadian Patent Office (Commissioner of Patents), including PCT national phase and sequence listing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOPOP is guidance only; follow legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: This Manual of Patent Office Practice (MOPOP) sets out CIPO's interpretation of the Patent Act, the Patent Rules and jurisprudence and is a guide only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are inconsistencies between the information in this manual and the applicable legislation, the legislation must be followed. The manual is not legally binding and should not be relied upon for legal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for patent protection, your invention must be: new—first in the world; useful—functional and operative; inventive—showing ingenuity and not obvious to someone of average skill in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inventions include products, compositions, machines, processes and improvements. Public disclosure before filing may bar patentability (with a limited 1-year exception for disclosures by the inventor in Canada). First-to-file rule applies in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing written communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All written communications intended for the Commissioner of Patents or the Patent Office must be addressed to the Commissioner of Patents (section 6 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent agent submits the communication on behalf of an applicant/patentee, the communication must include the name of the patent agent unless the agent is taking an action that may be taken by any person authorized by an applicant or patentee (section 41.1). Each communication must, subject to exceptions, pertain to a single application/patent and must identify the application/patent number and applicant/patentee name(s) (sections 8 and 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person doing business with the Patent Office via written communication must always provide their postal address (section 7 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications sent to the provided postal or email address are considered sent to that person on the date they bear; keep address records current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary communications with the Commissioner must be in English or French to allow the Office to provide basic service (section 15 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain documents may be in other languages (e.g., reference at filing to a previously filed application, the specification and drawings at filing, copies of priority applications, sequence listing text), though translations will generally be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-application communication exception list
rubrics_metrics.description: Written communications are permitted to relate to more than a single patent application or patent if the communication pertains to specific matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted multi-application matters include changes in name and address; transfers; requests to register documents; payment of maintenance fees; appointments or revocations of agent; and correction of an error that is the same in each application or patent (subsection 8(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying an application when number unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent application number is not known, sufficient information must be given to identify that application (subsection 9(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will attempt to identify the application but its databases have limited search functions — applicants are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for paper documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted in paper form must comply with section 13 of the Patent Rules and be suitable for optical scanning and storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper documents must be on white paper free of creases and folds, sized 8.5 x 11 inches (21.6 x 27.9 cm) or A4 (21 x 29.7 cm), presented to permit direct reproduction, and free of interlineations, cancellations or corrections. See sections 47–52 for application-specific presentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may communicate with the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: There are specific Patent Rules requirements regarding who can communicate with the Patent Office for certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 5 for additional information on representation, common representatives, appointed patent agents and associate patent agents, and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating addresses and effect of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of applicants, patentees, or their representatives to maintain current and accurate postal/email addresses on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office sends a communication to the address on file, it will be considered sent on the date it bears. For returned communications the Office will verify the address and either resend a courtesy copy (if address correct) or withdraw and reissue with a new date (if address incorrect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical delivery options and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Written communications may be physically delivered by mail, in person, or to a designated establishment as outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office address for in-person or mail delivery is provided. Once communications are received by CIPO they cannot be returned. When submitting a fee, include the Fee Form and avoid including financial information on other documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated mail services accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: For physical delivery, the Commissioner designates Canada Post Registered Mail™ and Xpresspost™ services as accepted for submission of documents, information or fees (subsection 10(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use those services where appropriate to ensure accepted delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission is considered original
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents, information or fees submitted online or by facsimile constitute the original; therefore a duplicate paper copy should not be forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions must still comply with the electronic format requirements set out by the Office. Refer to Section 2.03 for receipt dating rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online filing channels
rubrics_metrics.description: CIPO provides specific online channels for submitting written communications and applications (regular filing, MyCIPO Patents, general correspondence, ordering copies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate online link/service for the type of submission (regular application, MyCIPO, general correspondence, document orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile correspondence must be sent only to the facsimile numbers specified by CIPO; the electronic transmittal report is the acknowledgment receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted fax numbers are (819) 953-CIPO (2476) or (819) 953-OPIC (6742). Facsimiles sent elsewhere will be considered not received. Confidentiality cannot be guaranteed; internet-based fax services are discouraged. If a fee is sent by fax, the Fee Form must prominently show preferred payment mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT e-filing and international correspondence practice
rubrics_metrics.description: CIPO, as Receiving Office/ISA/IPEA, accepts electronic filing of international (PCT) applications via ePCT and PCT E-Filing, and will send PCT international written communications by default to the postal address provided in form PCT/RO/101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initial filing, PCT-related documents/correspondence may be sent electronically via facsimile or CIPO's secure online form. To receive correspondence via Canada Post Connect applicants must provide a preferred email and a written signed consent form available on CIPO's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission on electronic media (physical media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted on electronic media (diskette, CD, DVD, etc.) must include a cover letter and table of contents; parts must be broken into files no larger than 25 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic media will be date-stamped and placed in the application file. Media must be free of viruses or malicious content; such files will be deleted. See Annex F of the PCT Administration Instructions for acceptable media formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable electronic file formats and technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Files submitted online or on electronic media must be in TIFF, PDF, or ASCII formats complying with detailed technical specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIFF: CCITT Group 4, single or multi-page black & white, 300 or 400 dpi, dimensions matching 8.5x11 or A4. PDF: Adobe PDF version 1.4 compatible, non-compressed searchable text, unencrypted, no embedded OLE objects, all fonts embedded and licensed. ASCII: encoded using IBM Code Page 437, IBM Code Page 932 or compatible. The Office may accept other formats viewable with Stellent Quick View Plus 8.0.0 but will request replacement by TIFF or PDF with an explanation of identical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic form of sequence listings (ST.26 XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a sequence listing is required under section 58 of the Patent Rules, the sequence listing must be presented in electronic form and comply with the PCT sequence listing standard (Annex C/ST.26 XML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As Receiving Office, Canada accepts sequence listings submitted in Annex C/ST.26 compliant XML at filing (as part of the electronic application) or subsequent filing as permitted by PCT rules. See Part 7 of the PCT Administrative Instructions for details on labelling and fee calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for written communications from the Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents or the Patent Office will send written communications to the postal or email address provided by the correspondent; default is postal unless email is specifically requested and authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When correspondence pertains to a particular application/patent and all agents at a firm are appointed, correspondence sent to the firm is considered sent to all agents (section 29.1). See Chapter 5 for representation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for returned communications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a communication from the Office is returned, the Office will verify the address on file and act accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recorded address is correct the Office will resend a courtesy copy and any consequences will stand. If the address is incorrect the Office will withdraw and reissue the communication with a new date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for allegations of missing communications (applicant alleges non-receipt)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant alleges they did not receive a written communication sent by the Office, the Office will conduct an internal review and may require an affidavit/statutory declaration with evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office establishes the communication was sent to the correct recorded address it may withdraw the communication if supported by affidavit/statutory declaration demonstrating non-receipt. If satisfied that the communication was not received, the Office will withdraw and reissue with a new date; otherwise it will consider the communication received. Remedies for consequences (abandonment, deemed expiry) may include seeking reinstatement under the Patent Act or reversal of deemed expiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for erroneous communications originating from the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office inadvertently sends Notices for actions that are not or no longer prescribed, the Office will notify the recipient that such notices will be considered never sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include notices for non-payment of maintenance fee on applications already beyond reinstatement or withdrawn. The Office will consider any effects produced by those notices never to have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for allegations of missing communications sent to the Office (external client claims delivered)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person alleges they submitted a communication to the Office but the item appears not to have been received by CIPO, the Office will consider an affidavit or statutory declaration with documentary evidence supporting reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence may include indications of reception or payment. If satisfied the Office received the item on a specified date, the Office will deem it received on that date. Re-submission of the documents will also be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for alleged delayed receipt of examiner's report
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant alleges an examiner's report was received more than one month after its date, the Office may withdraw the report provided certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must file a requisition under subsection 86(2) or 86(5) (or contain a requisition/requirement under sections 85, 85.1 or 94), and submit an affidavit/statutory declaration with evidence within 14 days of receipt of the report. If satisfied, the Office will withdraw and issue a new report. Alternatively, the applicant may request an extension of time to respond under subsection 3(1) of the Patent Rules.
